probes.author: r3x-tortoise-orm-drafter
probes.query: When rows come back from the database, the library turns some column values into Python values with a conversion routine owned by the field kind, turns others with a plain call of the Python type, and leaves the rest exactly as the driver gave them. Trace where this three-way split is decided, what facts it uses (including what differs between SQLite, PostgreSQL and the remaining engines), how a field kind can ask to skip its own routine, when the decision is computed, and which other kind of query reuses it.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: Model._init_from_db fills each loaded column from one of three precomputed lists on the model meta: db_native_fields (value assigned as the driver returned it), db_default_fields (value passed through the field's Python type unless None) and db_complex_fields (value passed through the field's own to_python_value).

CRITICAL: MetaInfo._generate_db_fields makes the split: a field is native when its field_type is in the executor class's DB_NATIVE set and it either does not override to_python_value or sets skip_to_python_if_native; it is 'default' when it does not override to_python_value; otherwise it is 'complex'.

The DB_NATIVE set is engine specific: the base executor lists bytes, str, int, float, Decimal, datetime and date; the SQLite executor narrows it to bytes, str, int, float; the PostgreSQL-family executor adds bool and UUID to the base set.

Only DecimalField, DateField and TimeField set skip_to_python_if_native to True (the base Field default is False); DatetimeField overrides to_python_value without the flag, so it stays 'complex' on every engine.
The split is computed per model in MetaInfo.finalise_model (via _generate_db_fields), which Apps._build_initial_querysets calls after the connection (and so its executor class) is known.
FieldSelectQuery.resolve_to_python_value returns an identity function for fields in db_native_fields, and the values()/values_list() queries use it when converting result columns.
probes.notes: VERIFICATION: models.py:821 Model._init_from_db loops meta.db_native_fields (raw setattr), db_default_fields (field.field_type(value) if not None), db_complex_fields (field.to_python_value); KeyError fallback at models.py:846-862 handles .only() partial rows. models.py:473-490 MetaInfo._generate_db_fields (is_native_field_type = field.field_type in self.db.executor_class.DB_NATIVE; default_converter = field.__class__.to_python_value is Field.to_python_value). models.py:311-318 finalise_model; apps.py:118 Apps._build_initial_querysets calls it (state_apps.py:105 has a StateApps twin). DB_NATIVE: backends/base/executor.py:42, backends/sqlite/executor.py:26, backends/base_postgres/executor.py:74; MySQL/ODBC define none. fields/data.py:351 DecimalField, :532 DateField, :568 TimeField set skip_to_python_if_native=True; fields/base.py:198 default False. TimeField flag is inert (datetime.time is in no DB_NATIVE set); UUIDField overrides to_python_value (data.py:840) without the flag so UUID is 'complex' even on PostgreSQL. queryset.py:1709 FieldSelectQuery.resolve_to_python_value identity-lambda for db_native_fields; used at queryset.py:1868 (ValuesListQuery._execute) and :2000 (ValuesQuery._execute, which drops LambdaType columns). DECOYS: Field.to_python_value / DatetimeField.to_python_value (single-field conversion), BaseExecutor.execute_select (just calls _init_from_db), Field.skip_to_python_if_native docstring in fields/base.py. ROUTE: (1) grep to_python_value/_init_from_db -> read Model._init_from_db, sees meta.db_native_fields etc [G]; (2) grep db_native_fields -> MetaInfo._generate_db_fields + FieldSelectQuery [G]; (3) read _generate_db_fields, sees executor_class.DB_NATIVE and skip_to_python_if_native [G], grep both; (4) read the three executors and the three data.py classes [G]; (5) grep finalise_model/_generate_db_fields callers -> apps.py [G]. MIN CALLS: 5 (the values-query hop and the finalise_model hop ride along in calls 2 and 3 once the names are seen). FIRST CALL: grep 'to_python_value', grep '_init_from_db', grep 'executor' in tortoise/, grep 'native', grep 'values_list' -> reaches models.py, queryset.py, fields/data.py (3 gold files), so the first call is already broad; est. turns 7.

probes.author: r3x-tortoise-orm-drafter
probes.query: A query asks the library to bring related records along with the main records in a single database round trip. Trace how it works from the request method to the finished objects: where the request is recorded, where and how the join and the extra columns are added, what bookkeeping is kept about the column layout, and how one flat result row is cut back into several objects that are linked to each other. Include what happens when the related row is missing and when the same query also restricts which fields to load.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: QuerySet.select_related only adds the requested names to a set; the joins and extra columns are created later in QuerySet._make_query, which calls _join_select_related for each name after ordering and filters are resolved.

_join_select_related expands the double-underscore path with expand_lookup_expression and joins every hop through _join_table_by_field (get_joins_for_related_field), using a LEFT OUTER JOIN that is de-duplicated through the list of already joined tables.

For each hop it appends a tuple (related model, number of the model's db fields, field name, parent model, path) to _select_related_idx and selects the related columns aliased as '<table alias>.<column>'.
QuerySet._execute passes _select_related_idx to the executor, and BaseExecutor.execute_select slices each flat row into consecutive chunks using the recorded counts.

CRITICAL: For each related chunk execute_select strips the alias prefix (split on the first dot), builds the related object with that model's _init_from_db, finds the parent by path and attaches the object by setting a private underscore-prefixed attribute with object.__setattr__.

If every value in a related chunk is falsy the related object is None (LEFT JOIN found nothing); a count of 0, produced by _resolve_only for a nested only() field, creates an empty placeholder instance; when only() restricts fields, _join_select_related adds no related columns itself.
probes.notes: VERIFICATION: queryset.py:1048 QuerySet.select_related adds to self._select_related; :1268 _make_query resets _select_related_idx, resolves ordering/filters, then at :1309-1311 loops self._select_related calling :1150 _join_select_related (expand_lookup_expression from query_utils.py:88, _join_table_by_field queryset.py:190 -> get_joins_for_related_field query_utils.py:32, _join_table :198 uses JoinType.left_outer dedup via _joined_tables; append_item tuple at :1167-1174; alias f'{table.get_table_name()}.{related_field}' at :1181; 'continue' for _fields_for_select at :1163-1165). :1183 _resolve_only builds idx entries with len(data_fields) or 0 (comment about filler objects). :1330-1337 _execute passes select_related_idx=self._select_related_idx. backends/base/executor.py:111-157 execute_select: _split_cache with k.split('.',1)[1] (:140), 'if any(v for _, v in related_items)' builds obj via model._init_from_db, 'elif index == 0' empty filler, else None; object.__setattr__(target, f'_{attr}', obj). DECOYS: prefetch_related path (BaseExecutor._execute_prefetch_queries / _do_prefetch) which issues separate queries; Model._fk_getter (reads the underscore attribute; intentionally NOT asked, overlaps held-out r3-12); QuerySet._make_query of other query classes. ROUTE: (1) grep select_related in queryset.py -> :1048 stores set only [G: term _select_related]; (2) read _make_query -> sees _join_select_related and _select_related_idx [G]; (3) read _join_select_related -> _join_table_by_field, expand_lookup_expression, alias format [G]; grep those -> query_utils.get_joins_for_related_field + _join_table; (4) _execute passes select_related_idx to executor [G] -> grep select_related_idx in backends/ -> execute_select; (5) read execute_select for splitting rules; (6) read _resolve_only for the only() interplay. MIN CALLS: 5. FIRST CALL: grep 'select_related', grep 'join', grep 'only(', grep 'LEFT', grep 'related' in tortoise/ -> reaches queryset.py (1 gold file) plus many noise hits in docs and fields/relational.py; est. turns 7.

probes.author: r3x-tortoise-orm-drafter
probes.query: A test helper gives each run its own freshly created database on a server engine, while a file-based engine just works. Explain how a unique database name is produced from the connection address, how the request to create the database travels from the helper down to the call that creates it, how the creating step differs per engine (including what it connects to before the database exists), and what happens to the database when the helper exits.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: tortoise_test_context builds its config with generate_config(..., testing=True), which calls expand_db_url(testing=True); there the database path has backslash-escaped braces unescaped and is then str.format-ed with a fresh uuid4 hex, so a '{}' placeholder in the address path becomes a unique name (a path without placeholder, like an in-memory SQLite address, stays unchanged).
The helper then calls ctx.init(config=..., _create_db=True) followed by generate_schemas(safe=False); TortoiseContext.init forwards the flag to ConnectionHandler._init(config, create_db).
ConnectionHandler._init runs _init_connections, which obtains each connection with get(alias) and awaits its db_create() when the create flag is set.

CRITICAL: Server-engine db_create implementations first call create_connection(with_db=False) so the connection template carries no database name (asyncpg database None, psycopg dbname None, MySQL db None), then execute CREATE DATABASE (PostgreSQL adds OWNER of the configured user) and close the connection.
SQLite's db_create does nothing because the file is created when first connected.
On exit TortoiseContext.__aexit__ only closes the connections (close_all with discard) and clears apps; it never drops the database, because db_delete is called only from Tortoise._drop_databases.

OWNER; close); asyncpg/client.py:41-48 template 'database': self.database if with_db else None; psycopg/client.py ~:84-100 dbname=... if with_db else None; mysql/client.py:111-120 'db': self.database if with_db else None, :168 db_create; sqlite/client.py:107 db_create 'pass'. context.py:476-483 __aexit__ -> close_connections (:431-446) -> close_all(discard=True); no db_delete. __init__.py:513 Tortoise._drop_databases is the only db_delete caller. DECOYS: Tortoise._drop_databases/db_delete (cleanup path not used by the helper), contrib.test.init_memory_sqlite (different helper, no unique naming), TortoiseContext.generate_schemas. ROUTE: (1) grep tortoise_test_context / uuid -> read context.py helper [sees testing=True and _create_db=True: G]; (2) grep 'testing' in backends -> expand_db_url body [G]; (3) grep _create_db -> TortoiseContext.init and ConnectionHandler._init [G]; read _init_connections -> db_create [G]; (4) grep 'def db_create' -> per-engine bodies, read create_connection(with_db) in asyncpg/psycopg/mysql [G]; (5) grep db_delete/__aexit__ for teardown. probes.author: r3x-tortoise-orm-drafter
probes.query: A web application starts the ORM inside the web framework's startup hook, but incoming requests run in different tasks than the startup task, and queries still find the right database connections. Explain end to end how the startup helper asks for this, where the shared fallback is stored and guarded, how a model resolves its connection at request time, and why connections created at startup are visible in another task even though connection storage is per-task.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: RegisterTortoise defaults its global-fallback switch to True (Tortoise.init and TortoiseContext.init default it to False) and init_orm passes it into Tortoise.init, then also stores the context on app.state.

Tortoise.init takes the context from the context variable only; if there is none it creates a TortoiseContext and enters it, which sets the variable in the startup task alone; TortoiseContext.init ends by calling set_global_context(self) when the switch is on, and a second global context raises ConfigurationError.
get_current_context returns the context-variable value first and falls back to the module-level _global_context; require_context raises RuntimeError when neither exists.

A model finds its connection through MetaInfo.db -> get_connection(default_connection) -> require_context().connections.get(alias), so a request task without its own context variable resolves the startup context through the global fallback.

CRITICAL: ConnectionHandler keeps connections in a ContextVar whose default is one shared empty dict; startup creation writes into that default dict without calling set, so other tasks see the same connections, whereas transactions use set() with a copied dict that stays task-local.
Shutdown (close_orm -> Tortoise.close_connections -> TortoiseContext.close_connections) closes the handler and resets _global_context to None when it is that context.

DECOYS: transactions .set/.reset path (held-out r3-01 covers it, not asked); contrib/starlette, sanic, quart etc. (no fallback flag); tortoise.connections proxy (_ConnectionsProxy). ROUTE: (1) grep lifespan/startup in contrib/fastapi -> RegisterTortoise (flag default True) [G: _enable_global_fallback]; (2) grep _enable_global_fallback -> Tortoise.init and TortoiseContext.init, set_global_context [G]; (3) read context.py -> get_current_context/require_context [G]; grep require_context -> connection.get_connection [G]; (4) grep get_connection in models.py -> MetaInfo.db; (5) read ConnectionHandler._storage_var/get/set [G] for the shared default dict; (6) teardown in close_connections. MIN CALLS: 5. FIRST CALL: grep 'lifespan', grep 'startup', grep 'fastapi', grep 'ContextVar', grep 'global' -> reaches contrib/fastapi/__init__.py, context.py, connection.py (3 gold files; noisy); est. turns 7.

probes.author: r3x-tortoise-orm-drafter
probes.query: After the models are initialised, the library adds relation-related members that the developer never wrote. The migration system must not record them as the developer's own, and must be able to rebuild them later. Name each kind of automatically added member, say how each kind is marked, and list every place that sets the mark, skips such members when snapshotting or writing migration files, reads information back from them, recreates them when migrations are replayed, or skips them when tables are created.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: Apps._init_relations creates three kinds of automatic members: an integer key column named after the foreign key field plus _id whose reference attribute points back at that FK field (apps.py:193), a reverse relation on the target model (BackwardFKRelation or BackwardOneToOneRelation), and for many-to-many a reverse M2M field flagged _generated = True.
CRITICAL: ModelState.make_from_model skips all three kinds when snapshotting: instances of BackwardFKRelation, M2M fields with _generated, and any field whose reference is not None.
MigrationWriter._format_create_model additionally leaves out any field whose name equals another field's source_field, i.e. the generated key column of an FK.

ForeignKeyFieldInstance.deconstruct reads the real column name back from the generated key column (the field named by source_field) so the written file carries the column name the developer asked for.

On replay State._reload re-renders model classes from the states and calls apps._init_relations (StateApps._init_relations defers models whose target is not registered yet), which creates the automatic members again.

The schema editors' _get_m2m_table_definition (base, MySQL, MSSQL, Oracle) return None for a _generated reverse M2M so only the forward side creates the link table, and _get_model_sql_data uses a key column's reference to emit the FK definition.

DECOYS: backends/base/schema_generator.py (create-all path has its own _generated skip at _get_m2m_tables; not migration), OperationGenerator._sort_by_dependencies (r3h-07 held-out), ModelState.render. ROUTE: (1) grep BackwardFKRelation/make_from_model in migrations -> state.py:61 [G: reference, _generated]; (2) grep '\.reference' and '_generated' across tortoise/ -> apps.py, editors, sqlite editor [G]; (3) read apps.py _init_relations for the three creations; (4) read writer._format_create_model source_fields [G]; (5) read FK deconstruct comment and State._reload/StateApps [G]; (6) read editor _get_m2m_table_definition variants. probes.author: r3x-tortoise-orm-drafter
probes.query: On SQLite, a column for exact decimal numbers is stored as text, yet filtering, ordering, and arithmetic or aggregate expressions over it compare numerically. List every place in the library that causes this, including where the engine-specific column type and the conversion are declared, and how the right engine's variant is looked up and where the engine name comes from.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: DecimalField's inner _db_sqlite class declares SQL_TYPE VARCHAR(40) and a function_cast method that wraps the column term in Cast(..., NUMERIC); the base Field.function_cast default is None.

CRITICAL: Field.get_for_dialect looks up the inner _db_<dialect> class by name and returns the attribute (instantiating the class when the value is a property), falling back to the field's own attribute; the dialect string comes from model._meta.db.capabilities.dialect, which the SQLite client declares as 'sqlite'.
Filtering: Q._process_filter_kwarg wraps the column term with the function_cast result before applying the filter operator.
Ordering: AwaitableQuery.resolve_ordering wraps the ordered column the same way before orderby.
Expressions: F.resolve wraps a plain model-field reference, so arithmetic and annotations see the cast column.
Function and aggregate arguments: resolve_nested_field (query_utils) applies the cast to the last field of a nested path, which Function._resolve_nested_field uses.
probes.notes: VERIFICATION: fields/data.py:392-396 DecimalField._db_sqlite (SQL_TYPE='VARCHAR(40)', function_cast -> functions.Cast(term, SqlTypes.NUMERIC)); fields/base.py:200 Field.function_cast None; :404-408 get_db_field_type; get_for_dialect in base.py (property-aware lookup). Cast sites (only four in the library): expressions.py:167-173 F.resolve, expressions.py:414-419 Q._process_filter_kwarg, queryset.py:291-296 AwaitableQuery.resolve_ordering, query_utils.py:155-158 resolve_nested_field (called by expressions.py Function._resolve_nested_field :555-559). Dialect: backends/sqlite/client.py:~52-62 Capabilities('sqlite', ...); models.py:291 MetaInfo.db. DECOYS: backends/sqlite/executor.py sqlite3.register_adapter(Decimal, str) (write-side adapter, held-out r3h-08 gold, not part of the asked comparisons); DecimalField.to_python_value quantize (read-back); BaseExecutor.DB_NATIVE (read conversions); values()/select paths do not cast. ROUTE: (1) grep DecimalField/sqlite in fields/data.py -> _db_sqlite [G: function_cast]; (2) grep function_cast across tortoise/ -> four consumer sites + base.py docs [G]; (3) read get_for_dialect in fields/base.py; (4) read each consumer body (expressions.py x2, queryset.py, query_utils.py); (5) capabilities.dialect source in sqlite client. MIN CALLS: 4 (honest; this is the easiest of the set). probes.author: r3x-tortoise-orm-drafter
probes.query: A model declares an index that has a specific kind (for example a text-search or hash kind) and, for some index classes, a row-filter condition. Explain what SQL each of SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle ends up with for the kind and the condition, both when all tables are created from the model classes and when the index is added by a migration step. Name the code that makes each engine behave differently.
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: An Index carries its kind in INDEX_TYPE and a free text in extra; PartialIndex builds extra as ' WHERE col = value AND ...' from its condition dict and FullTextIndex sets extra to ' WITH PARSER <name>'.

Create-all path: BaseSchemaGenerator._get_field_indexes_sqls calls Index.get_sql, which calls _get_index_sql with the kind and extra; the base template (used by SQLite) puts the kind before the INDEX keyword and the extra at the end, so both appear.
PostgreSQL (generator and migration editor) rewrites the kind into 'USING <kind>' placed after the table name and before the column list, and appends the extra, so the WHERE condition is honoured.
CRITICAL: The MSSQL and Oracle index templates have no slot for the kind or the extra (in both the generators and the editors), so both are silently dropped; their generators also force safe=False.
MySQL create-all: _get_index_sql stores the SQL in _field_indexes and returns an empty string, and _get_inner_statements places it inside CREATE TABLE as '<kind>KEY `name` (cols)<extra>'.

Migration path differences: the base editor template has {extra} but no {index_type}, so SQLite loses the kind there while keeping WHERE; MySQLSchemaEditor.add_index builds its own CREATE <kind> INDEX statement and ignores extra.

Migration editors: schema_editor/base.py:20 template has {extra} only, :196-211 _get_index_sql, :396-417 _get_model_sql_data passes index.field_names/INDEX_TYPE/extra, :804-813 add_index; base_postgres.py:12-15 and :73-91 USING; mysql.py:16 template, :87-104 inline store, :217-225 add_index builds CREATE {type}INDEX without extra; mssql.py:21 and oracle.py:18 templates without slots (no _get_index_sql override). DECOYS: tuple-style indexes (plain field lists) path in _get_field_indexes_sqls; Index.index_name / _get_index_name (naming, r3-26 dev); contrib/postgres/indexes.py classes only set INDEX_TYPE; unique indexes (UNIQUE_INDEX_CREATE_TEMPLATE, extra=''). probes.author: r3x-tortoise-orm-drafter
probes.query: When many new objects are saved in one bulk call and the model has a database-generated integer key, some objects arrive with the key already filled in by the caller while others leave it empty. How does the library decide what each object's insert looks like, how many different insert statements can result for one batch, what happens to the keys the database generates, and which engine-specific piece changes the statement text?
expectedFacts: CRITICAL: Model._set_kwargs marks an instance with _custom_generated_pk = True when a value is passed for a key field that is both primary key and generated; instances built without it, or loaded from the database, are not flagged for generated keys.

BaseExecutor.__init__ prepares two column lists and statements: regular_columns / insert_query without generated columns, and regular_columns_all / insert_query_all with the generated columns included, built with has_generated=False.

CRITICAL: BulkCreateQuery._execute_many walks each batch from chunk(objects, batch_size) and splits instances by that flag: flagged ones use the 'all' statement with their key value, the others use the plain statement; each non-empty group is sent through the client's execute_many, so one batch can produce two statements (sql() joins both with a semicolon for a mix).

The PostgreSQL-family executor's _prepare_insert_statement adds RETURNING for the generated fields when has_generated is true (the plain statement only), but bulk insert sends rows through execute_many/executemany, so returned values are discarded and generated keys are not set on the objects (BulkCreateQuery.__await__ returns None).
When no conflict options or omitted db-default columns apply, _make_queries returns the executor's prebuilt insert_query and insert_query_all unchanged.
